sentences.text: th (Passed on 13 day of August, 2018) Per P.K. Jaiswal, J:-

The petitioner who is pursuing LLB course has filed this Public Interest Litigation and prayed for the following relief :-
"(A) That the Respondents may kindly be directed to provide the Proper Infrastructure, Food Facilities and Transportation facilities to the student of IIT.

(B) That the IIT Administration may kindly be directed Give Proper representation to the students in Committee Constituted for the purpose of dealing with Students Issues. (C) That the High Level Committee may kindly be Constituted to hear/inquire the Grievances of the Student and further to provide solution to their genuine problems.

(D) That, the Respondents may kindly be directed to Consult the Students/
Representative before taking any decision with regard to Student Issues, specially Food and Transportation.
(E) That the Respondents may kindly be directed to complete the ongoing Construction in the Simrol Campus within the time bound period and to provide the safety measures immediately.

sentences.text: (F) That the complete record with regard to construction, Canteen and Transportation may kindly called for the kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court.
Further to appoint a Committee to inquire and take appropriate action against the erring persons responsible for mismanagement and irregularities in the campus.

(G) That any other Relief, which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit may also kindly given, along with Cost."
2.
The Indian Institute of Technology, Indore was constituted by the Act of the Parliament, ie., the Institutes of Technology Act, 1961 (hereinafter referred as 'the Act') and further amendment in 2012.
Section 2 of the Act provides that certain institutes to the institutions of the national importance.
IIT Indore is also a institute of National Importance and was established in Indore.
Initially it was started in the IET Campus of Devi Ahilya University, Indore.
Thereafter, it was shifted to the place allotted at Simrol, Khandwa Road.

3. According to the petitioner, the students community of IIT Indore has for the last one and half years continuously lodged complaints via official channels to the concerned authorities at IIT Indore regarding serious problems in quality of food as well as the high prices for food in the mess.
To support the aforesaid paper cutting has been filed.

It is also alleged that the institute has reduced the number of buses plying to and fro from the campus to parts of Indore city, which particularly impacts the female population and limits their productivity, which is against the spirit of the Justice Verma Committee (Bills of Rights, Part IV - Right to Secured Spaces), UGC and AICTE Regulation.

The IIT Indore continues to hold classes and laboratories in buildings that are under construction,
the status of the construction has not been upto the mark.
The students are forced to study in very pathetic condition.
Several buildings of the IIT are operating without Fireman's lifts of Fire Safety Centre, which is required under the aegis of National Building Code of India, 2016.
The Institution currently operates several committees without adequate student representation in violation of UGC Guidelines and Regulations on the matter.
The administration in the utter violation of the UGC Guidelines has not given proper representation to the students in different Committees.
Due to delay in construction of the IIT building the students are forced to study in the under constructed building.
As per news paper cutting there is mismanagement and irregularities in the IIT Indore and prayed for issuance of proper directions as prayed in para 11 of the writ petition.
4. Per contra, Shri P. Mathur, learned Senior counsel for the respondents No.2 and 3 has submitted that petitioner is misrepresenting this court.
The writ petition is based on the false premises.
The respondent - Institute is a premier educational Institute of the country having immense reputation globally.
The respondent - Institute is efficiently rendering quality services to its students.
The Institute never involves in any kind of illegal activities.

The petitioner has miserably failed to submit representation / letter to the respondent Institute highlighting his grievance in respect to the allegations raised in the petition; instead the petitioner has directly preferred the present writ petition just to malign the reputation of the Institute.
It is submitted that the guidelines issued by the UGC are not binding on the Institute.
The respondent - Institute is constantly delivering excellent educational services to the students from across the nation.

The writ petition is based on news-paper article containing incorrect and false fact and no effort has been made to verify the facts as mentioned in the said article and prayed for dismissal of the writ petition with exemplary cost.

sentences.text: As per reply, the respondent - Institute is taking decisions in accordance with its statute and bye law and every decision of the institute is based upon consultation and with consensus of the General Council of the students.

In respect of poor quality of food offered by the existing mess contractor,
the stand of the Institute is that the Institute has changed the mess contractor namely, Bhopal Caterers and appointed the new contractor, ie., Kanaka Food Management Services Pvt. Ltd. in consultation with the student community of the respondent - Institute.

entities.text: Kanaka Food Management Services Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Thereafter, the respondent - Institute has taken feedback from the student community in respect to the quality of food and services rendered by the new contractor.

6. The respondents No.2 and 3 very categorically denied that the student community ITT Indore from the last one and half years has continuously lodging the complaints via official channels to the concerned authorities.
The petitioner has not filed any copy of complaint lodged by the student community.
His entire case is based upon paper cutting / news paper item.

There is no documents on record, which would substantiate petitioner's contention regarding any sort of violation of law /
regulation by the Institute.
The respondent - Institute is already working upon a city bus stop outside the main gate of the Institute and the same shall be completed at the earliest.

In respect of applicability of UGS Rules and Regulations, their stand is that the respondent's action is based upon SENATE decision and it is SENATE, who is mandatory for 3SCI index paper publication for the better quality of publication of articles.
The respondent - Institute has formed an Internal Complaints Committee to redress the grievance of the students.

7. As per reply the students of IIT Indore are getting world class facilities and the Institute has never compromised with the safety measures including fire safety measures as per the requirement under the National Building Code of India 2016.

The Institute to ensure that the building constructed are of high quality engaged the services of M/s. MECON Ltd., (a reputed Project Management Consultancy Company) to supervise the progress of the construction work and ensure that the quality of construction of the building is as per the International Standard.

After completion of construction the completion/occupancy certificate (Annexure R/6) has been issued by the M/s.
MECON Ltd.
Their stand is that the Institute is operating several committees without adequate student representation.
The petitioner has not brought a single violation of any statutory norm/regulation and has merely made a bald allegation.
The respondent - Institute has provided student representations in various committees in the Institute.
The norms of the UGC are nor applicable on the respondent - Institute and they are bound by its own statute namely IIT Indore Statute.

8. The Public Interest Litigation is based on news-paper cutting and no representation or documents has been filed to prove that number of representations were made by the students of IIT,
Indore.
The petitioner is a law student, he has not filed any document to substantiate his grievance made in the writ petition.
9. It is well settled law that, there must be real and genuine public interest involved in the litigation and not merely an adventure of knight errant borne out of wishful thinking.
It cannot also be invoked by a person or a body of persons to further his or their personal causes or satisfy his or their personal grudge and enmity.

Courts of justice should not be allowed to be polluted by unscrupulous Harsh Wardhan Sharma vs Union Of India on 13 August, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79170483/
3 litigants by resorting to the extraordinary jurisdiction.

sentences.text: A person acting bona fide and having sufficient interest in the proceeding of public interest litigation will alone have a locus standi and can approach the court to wipe out violation of fundamental rights and genuine infraction of statutory provisions, but not for personal gain or private profit or political motive or any oblique consideration.
The present PIL is filed without thorough study of factual situation.
Nor specific pleadings are made to substantiate allegations.
10. For these reasons, we find no merit in the writ petition and the same is hereby dismissed without any cost.
